label: 01 / The design loop
title: Design starts with evidence and returns to it.
lead: I start by making the problem and intended outcome clear. A working prototype lets me test that intent. What I learn in testing and after release feeds the next decision.
caption: The outer arrows trace the five stages. Dashed lines link each stage to shared facts. The side panel shows who has the authority to decide.

notes.title: Keep the reasoning visible
notes.body: The spec, design system, and working agreements give everyone a common reference. When a test or production incident changes what the team knows, that evidence can be traced to the decision it affects.

notes.title: Carry the evidence forward
notes.body: In the workstation, I want to open a decision and see why it was made, what shipped, and whether it worked.

label: 02 / Code as a design material
title: Working with code changes what I can test.
lead: When a prototype runs, I can see what happens when data arrives late, a request fails, or a user lacks permission. As I move from building a demo to reviewing a change or helping ship it, the evidence I need changes too.
caption: Compare what each kind of work can demonstrate and what still needs evidence. The five checks apply at every stage.

notes.title: Match the evidence to the claim
notes.body: A demo can show that a flow works in the cases it covers. A targeted review tells me whether a particular change fixed the issue. A release decision calls for broader checks and approval from the people who own the risks.

notes.title: Show what is ready for review
notes.body: In the workstation, I want to see whether I’m looking at an experiment, a reviewed change, or a release candidate. Each should show what has been checked, what still needs evidence, and who can make the next decision.

label: 03 / Design system context
title: The design system gives agents rules they can check.
lead: An agent needs to know which component fits a situation, how it behaves in different states, and when it can be used. The design system can supply those rules and give the team a way to check the result.
alt: The design system as agent context
caption: Read from constraints through the agent workflow to the output checks. The outer arrows show how feedback returns to the design system.

notes.title: Give the agent usable rules
notes.body: I want rules that tell an agent how to choose a component, map it to code, handle its states, and recognize when a pattern is out of bounds.

notes.title: Make the result reviewable
notes.body: Each result should point to the version of the rules it used. If a review exposes a gap in those rules, the team can fix the source and verify the next result.

label: 04 / Delivery artifacts
title: A spec should explain how the work gets done.
lead: Once a prototype can act, I want the team to agree on three things before it moves forward. Who is responsible, what information the system can rely on, and what it is allowed to do.
caption: Roles, context, and permissions feed into the spec that guides implementation, integration, testing, and acceptance.

notes.title: Approval needs evidence
notes.body: In a purchase flow, the agent can draft a recommendation. A buyer needs the source data, the assumptions, and the proposed quantity before approving a commitment.

notes.title: Keep the spec current
notes.body: When a test reveals a missing permission or an unclear responsibility, I want that change reflected in the spec and linked to the version the team reviewed.

label: 05 / Human and agent access
title: People and agents need access to the same facts.
lead: A buyer needs a clear explanation and a way to take over. The agent needs to identify the right order, understand its state, and know which actions it can take. Both should be working from the same underlying record.
alt: Two ways to access the same facts
caption: The human interface and agent tools share the same product facts. Test both paths in the same task, including how they recover when something goes wrong.

notes.title: Test a complete task
notes.body: I want to see what the agent reads, what the buyer sees before approving, and how the result is recorded. If an action fails, both paths should give the team enough information to recover.

notes.title: Check accessibility on its own terms
notes.body: A reliable tool interface helps the agent operate. People still need an accessible interface and a clear way to understand, challenge, or take over a decision.

label: 06 / Team delivery
title: A successful prototype should teach the team something it can reuse.
lead: A working demo shows that an idea can be tried. Version history shows how the work changed. Methods tested across tasks help others repeat it. A release decision needs evidence from the running product and review by the people responsible for it.
alt: From individual prototypes to team delivery
caption: Four kinds of evidence support team delivery. Shared records and a log of key AI contributions let reviewers trace what changed and why.

notes.title: Record the decisions that matter
notes.body: I want enough context for a reviewer to see what the agent used, what it produced, what people changed, and how the result was tested.

notes.title: Make reuse a team practice
notes.body: When a pattern works across tasks, it can become a component, a template, or a reusable skill. Its source, limits, and verification should travel with it.

label: 07 / The workstation
title: One shared workspace. Four connected surfaces.
lead: This preview shows how I imagine the workstation could work, using Aurora Store as an example. Open AUR-8 to see how support evidence and a shared spec inform two versions of the shopping cart. The second version adds Undo after review.

notes.title: Evidence canvas
notes.body: Problem statements, source interviews, hypotheses, business outcomes, risk, and named decision owners.

notes.title: Constraint library
notes.body: Versioned tokens, components, semantic rules, behavior, permissions, and verified reusable patterns.

notes.title: Live lab
notes.body: Realistic prototype states, agent traces, code diffs, mocked or approved data, and observable recovery paths.

notes.title: Evaluation console
notes.body: Automated checks, expert review, test evidence, production signals, regression history, and authorization gates.

label: 08 / Operating principles
title: What I would hold the workstation to.
lead: A faster design process only matters when it improves the quality of decisions and the reliability of what reaches users.

notes.title: Every important decision has a reason.
notes.body: Keep evidence, assumptions, trade-offs, and approved constraints connected to the running artifact.

notes.title: Automation does not equal permission.
notes.body: Agents can prepare, recommend, and verify. A responsible person or authorized role still approves consequential actions.

notes.title: Make failure and recovery visible.
notes.body: Loading, empty states, errors, long data, access denial, responsiveness, and recovery are part of the design.

notes.title: Bring runtime evidence into the next decision.
notes.body: Events, failures, and user observations update the next hypothesis, the spec, and the design system itself.
